documents.title: Policies and Best Practices
documents.summary: The page collects existing data-protection rules and best practices for AI tools across the university and defers student AI-use rules to instructors and the Student Code of Conduct. Most content concerns data classification, vetted tools and accuracy checks.
documents.stance_why: The page mostly restates data-security and integrity policies and sets no AI-use stance of its own; students 'are expected to follow course-specific rules set by their instructors', so the decision sits with instructors.

units.policy: Students are expected to follow course-specific rules set by their instructors as well as academic integrity rules set by the university.

documents.title: Our Guiding Principles
documents.summary: Five university-wide guiding principles for AI covering mission, human agency, capacity building, innovation and lawful use. They are explicitly non-binding guideposts that leave local decisions to faculty, units and departments.
documents.stance_why: The principles state they 'are not intended to function as policy statements or a mandate' and say 'Faculty should decide how AI is used in their teaching', so no stance is set and decisions go to faculty and units.

documents.title: Teaching at Lehigh: Policies, Guidance, and Syllabus Statements

documents.stance_why: The provost page says 'Lehigh does not have a uniform policy about the allowable use of AI in courses' and tells instructors to set their own, so it delegates.

documents.title: Report and Recommendations from Lehigh's Generative AI Advisory Group

documents.stance_why: The report is an advisory group's recommendations, not binding policy; it urges departments to 'Develop clear AI usage guidelines' and supports faculty who 'lean into AI' or 'lean away', so decisions go to departments and faculty.
